distinct_mechanisms.explanation:
scripts/build_w5_eval_pool.py wrote JSON files using open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') without newline='
'. When executed on Windows during W5-PREP-01, Python translated '
' to '
' on disk and hashed those CRLF working-tree bytes immediately ( plus recorded the legacy CRLF Freeze V2 checksum 93681135...). When committed, root .gitattributes (* text=auto eol=lf) normalized the Git blobs to LF. Pure LF->CRLF conversion of the committed Git blobs reproduces all 5 hashes in w5_reproducibility_manifest_v1.json with zero content difference.

scripts/build_w5_annotation_package.py wrote Markdown and JSON files using open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') without newline='\n' (and without a trailing newline on JSON files). When executed on Windows during W5-PREP-02, Python wrote CRLF line endings to disk and hashed those CRLF bytes into w5_annotation_manifest_v1.json before Git normalized the committed blobs to LF. Pure LF->CRLF conversion of the committed Git blobs reproduces all 10 unique hashes (14 total entries) in w5_annotation_manifest_v1.json with zero content difference.

rec_eval_01_prereg_manifest_v1.json explicitly declares artifact_hash_basis = 'sha256_git_committed_blob_content' at source_commit_sha 35f82b30aa474d33036df656d70528dc20328d39. All 14 stored hashes match GIT_BLOB_BYTES_SHA256, WORKING_TREE_BYTES_SHA256, and LF_NORMALIZED_UTF8_SHA256 simultaneously.

Round 01 raw CSV submissions (J1, J2, J3 in raw_v1/ and inbox/) are governed by data/evaluation/reca_w5/calibration_submissions/.gitattributes (*.csv -text whitespace=cr-at-eol), which preserves the exact received CRLF bytes in both the Git blob and working tree on all platforms. Thus GIT_BLOB_BYTES_SHA256 == WORKING_TREE_BYTES_SHA256 == CRLF_NORMALIZED_UTF8_SHA256 for all 3 judges.

scripts/prepare_w5_calibration_round02.py explicitly writes LF-only files (newline='\n' / lineterminator='\n') and records both COMMITTED_GIT_BLOB_UTF8_LF_NORMALIZED_SHA256 and CANONICAL_SORTED_COMPACT_JSON_UTF8_SHA256. All 7 control artifacts and 3 contracts reproduce 100% identically across Git blobs, working tree, LF normalization, and canonical JSON.
